name: Psychedelic Card Table
summary: A Balatro-like card table: a flowing paint swirl floor, wobbling pixel cards and chip tokens, foil and holo editions, burn dissolves and a CRT screen.
description: The floor is one big slow paint swirl: three shades of one table colour (green felt by default, crimson and violet patches) poured and twisted like a lava lamp, rendered on the art-pixel grid. Everything on it is crisp pixel art in the language of a card table: a walking playing card with a jester hat, chip tokens with faces, flipping tarot cards, chip stacks, decks, dice and standing cards that shimmer in foil, holographic, polychrome or negative editions. Nothing ever just appears or changes: it wobbles (the 'juice' spring), pops square particles and rounded counter bubbles, burns away with a glowing edge, and the whole picture sits behind a curved CRT glass with scanlines, a chromatic fringe and bloom. In the spirit of the visual language of Balatro.
bestFor: menus, shops and reward screens that need juice
top-down arcade action with a playful tone
any project that wants a strong CRT pixel identity
avoidFor: projects that need soft lighting and 3D depth
high-density UI where screen distortion hurts readability

difficulty.why: Sprites are small, flat pixel art (cards are rounded rectangles with a 1 px edge, tokens are discs with notches) and need no shading beyond one highlight row, so new pieces are quick. The look lives in a handful of reusable systems – the swirl shader, the juice spring, silhouette shadows, edition shaders, dissolve and the CRT pass – which you write once and then apply to every new asset.

technique.renderer: Canvas 2D for sprites, particles and UI plus two WebGL2 fragment shaders: the paint swirl (rendered per frame into the art buffer) and the CRT post pass (over the final display image). A CPU swirl at quarter resolution and a 2D scanline/vignette overlay are the fallback.
technique.resolution: Art buffer of 1 art pixel per world unit (360 units tall), integer-upscaled with nearest neighbour to the screen (3x at 900 px). Sprites rotate and scale inside the art buffer, so the art-pixel grid is kept even on tilted cards.
technique.summary: A domain-warped paint swirl (five sin/cos warp iterations, then three colour weights from the length of the warped vector) fills the floor; flat pixel sprites with a 1 px ink outline sit on it with offset silhouette shadows; every reaction is a decaying spring wobble (scale sin(50.8 t), rotation sin(40.8 t), 0.4 s); a final CRT shader bends and fringes the whole image.
technique.linework: Every sprite (characters, props, tokens, icons) gets a 1 art-pixel outline in ink #24302f made by dilating the silhouette (4-neighbour, no diagonals). Cards additionally have a 1 px light edge #bfc7d5 inside the outline and 1 px cut corners. No anti-aliasing anywhere in the art buffer.
technique.shading: Flat fills. Cards get one lighter shade row on their right and bottom edge (#e6eaf0); chips get a darker side band (main colour x0.68); tokens are concentric discs (rim, white ring, dark centre). Volume comes from the drop shadow, not from gradients.
technique.lighting: No light direction in the world. Brightness comes from the swirl's own highlight term (lighting 0.28 adds white where a paint colour peaks), from white hit flashes, gold sparkles and the CRT bloom (mip-blurred image added where it is brighter than 0.3).
technique.texture: None on sprites. Editions add animated per-pixel patterns (foil bands, holographic rainbow grid, polychrome hue flow, negative inversion). The CRT adds a fine 2 px noise (±1.5 %) and one scanline per art-pixel row.

paletteRules: The table is always ONE base colour turned into three shades (x0.9 / x1.3 / x0.7) – never three unrelated hues on the floor.
Blue means 'adds a little', red means 'multiplies' – keep that pairing for counters, bubbles and tokens (blue + sign, red X sign).
Gold is money and reward only: coins, notches, sparkles, titles.
Sprites are flat saturated colours with an ink outline; the only gradients in the whole look are the swirl and the CRT.
White is the brightest thing on screen (cards, flashes, text) – keep the swirl highlight below it.
UI is dark slate (#3a5055 / #26353a) with white text and one saturated accent per element.

typography.role: All UI text: titles (75 px, gold), counters (42-47 px), card names (29 px), body copy on white boxes (21 px, #374244) – a pixel display face close to m6x11
Floating numbers inside popup bubbles, drawn as bitmaps on the art grid (0-9, +, X, $)
typography.css: /* drawn on the canvas: 3x5 px glyphs, 1 px spacing, white */

world.summary: An endless table covered by one slow paint swirl in three shades of the local table colour, with a few dark translucent card zones (some with dashed outlines and empty card slots). The swirl flows constantly and twists around the centre of the screen; its colours ease towards the table patch under the camera (green felt, crimson, violet, rare teal).
layers: Swirl: per art pixel, world position -> bounded coordinates p = (0.26 sin(x/150) + 0.2 sin((0.6x+0.8y)/131+1.3), 0.26 sin(y/150+0.7) + 0.2 sin((0.6y-0.8x)/127+2.1)); rotate p by a = spin - 20 (0.25 l + 0.75) with l = distance from the screen centre / 612; scale by 30; five domain-warp iterations driven by flow = time x 7; weights c1/c2/c3 from the warped length

Colours: base colour of the table patch (low-frequency noise, 1500-1900 units); swirl colours base x0.9, x1.3, x0.7; contrast 1.4 on felt, up to 2.3 on crimson; the live floor eases to the patch under the camera at rate 1.4/s

Card zones on a 230-unit grid (30 % of cells): rounded rectangles 60-116 x 44-72 units filled rgba(0,0,0,.13); 45 % get a dashed white outline (3 px dashes every 6 px, alpha .13); 40 % get 2-4 empty card slots 22 x 30 at rgba(0,0,0,.12)
Baked chunks (wide views) use the same swirl at rest (flow 0, no twist) evaluated every 2 x 2 art pixels with per-pixel patch colours, plus the zones

characters.summary: Pixel-art card table pieces brought to life, 1 px ink outline, flat colours, offset silhouette shadows. The main character (21 x 33 art px) is a walking playing card: white card body 15 x 19 with a light edge, red corner pips, two ink eyes, pink cheeks and a wide red grin with white teeth, white glove dots on ink arms, ink legs with a red and a blue shoe, and a two-pointed jester hat (red flap left, blue flap right, gold band, gold bells). Creatures: chip tokens (small, 17 px: blue, orange or green rim with 8 white notches, white ring, dark centre with a simple face), flipping tarot cards (fast, 13 x 18: violet back with a gold star, white front with a diamond pip, flipping by squeezing their width) and a large crimson token (34 px) with 12 gold notches, a gold ring and one glaring eye under angry brows.
rules: Every creature is a table object: a card, a chip or a token. Faces are minimal (dots and a line) so the object stays readable as the object.
Motion is springy, not frame-heavy: 4 walk frames for the card, 2 notch rotations for tokens; the rest is rotation, squash and the juice wobble applied to the whole sprite.
Chip tokens hop: height |sin(phase)| x 5, squash 1.12 x 0.86 on landing, tilt sin(phase) x 0.1.
Flipping cards hover 10-12 units up, turn by scaling x with |cos(4.2 t)|, showing the back while cos < 0, and tilt with the flip.
The large token sways ±0.08 rad, pulses ±2 % and has four bright pixels running around its rim.
Hit: a white silhouette for the flash plus the juice wobble (amount 0.4). Vanish: burn dissolve with a glowing edge and embers. Appear: the same dissolve in reverse with a white-to-blue edge.

props.summary: Table clutter as scenery, placed in small groups on a 150-unit grid (50 % of cells): chip stacks (4-8 chips, one or two colours, white edge stripes), coin piles, standing playing cards (A-K in four suits, gently swaying) that may shimmer in an edition, red decks with a visible thickness, white dice in 3/4 view, tarot cards (sun or moon), crimped booster packs with a holographic shimmer and small houses of cards.
rules: Props are the same pixel language as the characters: 1 px ink outline, card corners cut by 1 px, flat colours, one shade row.
Standing cards, tarot cards and packs sway ±0.025-0.04 rad; nothing else moves.
Editions on props: 20 % foil, 12 % holographic, 10 % polychrome, 6 % negative for standing cards; packs are always holographic; tarot cards 40 % foil.
Props cast the same offset silhouette shadow as characters; there are no contact ellipses anywhere.
Keep the table tidy: props come in clusters with lots of empty swirl between them.

effects.name: Square particles
effects.how: The signature particle: a square of 2-3 art px in a counter colour or white, rotating (±5-7 rad/s) and shrinking with (1 - k²) to nothing; bursts of 3 (impact), 8 (vanish), 18 (glow-up) with drag 3.

effects.name: Popup bubble
effects.how: A pill 10 px tall in blue (+N), red (XN) or gold ($N) with a 1 px darker lower lip (colour x0.68), a 1 px drop shadow and white 3x5 digits; pops in with outBack over 20 % of its life, wobbles with the juice formula, rises 8 units and shrinks away in the last 20 %.

effects.name: Burn dissolve
effects.how: Per sprite a noise mask (fbm at 1/5 px scale, plus 22 % bias towards the edges); a threshold sweeps from -0.08 to 1.1 in 12 cached steps; pixels below it vanish, a 0.09 wide band above it is painted from pale gold #ffe8a0 to red; embers (1 px orange/red) rise from the edge.

effects.name: Editions
effects.how: Foil: desaturate 60 % towards a blue-silver tint, add bands sin((1.4u - v) 10 + t) x rings sin(24 r - t), cubed. Holographic: rainbow hue along u+v plus a grid every 4th column / 5th row. Polychrome: hue rotated by 0.45 sin(4u + t) + 0.45 cos(5v - t) + 1.4 r, saturation at least 0.45. Negative: inverted colours tinted violet with a diagonal sheen. 8 frames baked per sprite; outlines stay ink.

effects.name: Collectibles
effects.how: Small: a gold coin 7 x 7 that spins by width (7, 5, 3, 5 px at 8 frames/s) and bobs 1.5 units. Large: a cyan mini card with a planet disc in the polychrome edition, tilting ±0.15 rad, with a twinkling white plus sparkle.

effects.name: Thrown card
effects.how: A 5 x 7 white mini card with a red cross pip, spinning at 14 rad/s, with a trail of three shrinking white/edge-grey squares behind it.

effects.name: Orbiting tokens
effects.how: Alternating blue (+) and red (X) 11 px tokens that spin by squeezing their width with |cos(5t)| and flash a white pixel now and then.

effects.name: Glow-up
effects.how: A ring of 18 squares in gold/white/red/blue flying outward, six plus-sparkles, an expanding dotted gold ring, a red X2 bubble above, a ring of gold squares turning around the character, and a burst of speed in the floor swirl.

atmosphere.summary: The picture is a CRT: barrel-curved glass with dark rounded corners, chromatic fringe that grows towards the edges, a soft bloom, one scanline per art-pixel row, a little noise and a vignette. Shadows are offset silhouettes. The floor swirl breathes faster on big moments.
rules: CRT pass (WebGL2 over the finished display image): p *= 1 + 0.045 |p|² - 0.018; outside the curved rectangle is black with an 0.8 % soft edge; chromatic offset (uv - 0.5) x 0.004 plus 0.45 px horizontally, red out / blue in.
Bloom: two mip levels (log2(upscale) + 1.5 and +2 more) averaged, everything above 0.3 added at 55 %.
Scanlines: cosine per art-pixel row darkening by up to 20 %, less on bright pixels (x (1 - 0.55 luminance)). Noise ±1.5 % on a 2 px grid. Vignette mixed in at 55 % from smoothstep(1.6, 0.45, r).

Shadows: the sprite's own silhouette in black at 33 % alpha, offset 3 units down and 1 unit plus (x - camera) x 0.025 sideways (max ±6), with the same rotation and scale as the sprite; lifted objects push the shadow further.
Swirl energy: big moments add to a pulse that speeds up the flow (x3) and rotates the swirl; it decays at 1.8/s.
No fog, no light map, no colour grading – the swirl and the CRT carry the whole mood.

ui.summary: Chunky rounded slate panels with a darker lip below and a hard offset drop shadow, dark inner wells for values, saturated pill counters (blue and red with an inner bottom shade and a top highlight), white text with a hard dark text shadow, white description boxes with dark text, red circular number badges, and cards that deal in with an overshoot and tilt on hover. Titles wobble slowly.

motion: Juice (every reaction): scale += A sin(50.8 t) ((0.4 - t)/0.4)³, rotation += A/2 sin(40.8 t) ((0.4 - t)/0.4)², over 0.4 s; A = 0.35-0.45 for hits, 0.12-0.25 for small events.
Main character: 4 walk frames at anim x 1.2, tilt sin(anim x 0.6π) x 0.07 while walking, idle sway ±0.025 rad and breathing ±1.5 % scale; leaning with horizontal speed (vx x 0.0006, max ±0.12).
Dash: two blue silhouettes 8 units apart at alpha 0.22/0.44 plus three red/blue echo silhouettes left as particles, and white squares blown backwards.
Swirl: flow = time x 7 (x up to 3 during a pulse), colours ease to the table patch at 1.4/s.
Dissolve 0.35 s in 12 steps; appear 0.5 s in reverse; hit flash while the flash value is above 0.4.
Particles: drag 3, life 0.35-0.8 s; bubbles 0.8-1.0 s; plus-sparkles 0.2 s.
UI: cards deal in from 70 px below with 9° tilt and scale 0.6 over 0.55 s (staggered 0.09 s) with an overshoot curve; hover lifts 10 px, tilts -2° and scales 1.05; titles wobble ±1.6° every 2.4 s.
do: Put every sprite on the art-pixel grid and rotate/scale it inside the low-res buffer, so tilted cards stay pixel art.
Give every reaction the juice wobble – hits, pickups, spawns, UI hovers.
Use the sprite's own silhouette as its shadow, offset down and away from the screen centre.
Keep the floor one colour family and change the whole table colour for a new area or moment.
Show values as blue (+) and red (X) bubbles and counters; gold for money.
Let things burn away with a glowing edge instead of just disappearing.
Finish with the CRT pass – curvature, fringe, bloom and scanlines are part of the identity.
dont: Don't use soft ellipse shadows or ambient occlusion – shadows are hard offset silhouettes.
Don't smooth or anti-alias the art buffer; never draw sprites at a non-integer upscale.
Don't fill the floor with detail – the swirl needs room, props come in small clusters.
Don't mix many hues on the table at once or put a second pattern over the swirl.
Don't animate with long frame sequences; use springs, squash and rotation.
Don't use thin or elegant fonts – everything is chunky pixel type with a hard shadow.
Don't let the swirl highlight get brighter than the white cards.
performance: Sprites, edition frames (8 per sprite), icons and bubbles are baked once at init; dissolve frames are built lazily and cached per sprite and step (12). Per frame: one WebGL2 draw for the swirl at art resolution (about 534 x 300 px), one texture upload plus mipmap and one draw for the CRT at display resolution, the rest is Canvas 2D drawImage. Without WebGL the swirl runs on the CPU at quarter resolution every second frame (a few milliseconds) and the CRT becomes a scanline pattern plus a radial vignette. Baked floor chunks evaluate the swirl every 2 x 2 art pixels (~16k samples per 256-unit chunk, spread over frames).
